definition: An optimizer that updates each parameter using running averages of its gradient and of the squared gradient. The training lab uses it. It is the step rule that turns gradients into weight changes.
A small set of extra trainable weights, such as a LoRA pair A and B, that is added to a frozen model. When you fine-tune this way, only the adapter needs to be saved.
A mechanism in which each token computes weights over the tokens it is allowed to see and returns a weighted mix of their values. It is how information moves between positions.
The procedure that computes the gradient of the loss with respect to every parameter by applying the chain rule backwards through the network.
A pretrained model that has learned to continue text but has not been tuned to follow instructions.
A group of training examples processed together in one forward and backward pass. Larger batches give steadier gradients but need more memory.
A pair of adjacent tokens. A bigram model predicts the next token from the one before it, using counts of pairs.
Byte-pair encoding, a method that builds a subword vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent pair of tokens.
A mask that stops each position from attending to later positions, so a token can only use what came before it. It is applied to the attention scores before the softmax.
The format that wraps messages, with roles and separators, into the single text string an instruct model was tuned on. Using the wrong template often makes answers worse.
Splitting long documents into smaller pieces so that retrieval can return only the relevant parts and they fit in the prompt.
The maximum number of tokens a model can take as input at one time. Text beyond this limit must be cut or left out.
The cosine of the angle between two vectors, computed as their dot product divided by the product of their lengths. It is 1 for vectors pointing the same way and 0 for perpendicular vectors.
The average negative log of the probability a model gives to the correct next token, taken over all positions. It is the training loss for language models.
A transformer that uses causal attention only and generates text one token at a time. A GPT is a decoder-only transformer.
A vector that represents a token or a piece of text. Learned embeddings place texts with similar meaning close together.
A fixed list of questions with reference answers, used to score a model. It is kept separate from the training data.
A scoring rule that counts an answer as correct only if it equals the reference after simple normalization such as case and spacing. It suits short factual answers.
Continuing to train a pretrained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset so that its behaviour changes.
An activation function that scales its input by the probability that a standard normal value is below it. The MLP in the tiny GPT uses a tanh approximation of it.
A single-file format that stores quantized model weights, the tokenizer and metadata together. The llama.cpp tools and runtimes built on them use it.
The vector of partial derivatives of the loss with respect to the parameters. It points in the direction in which the loss increases fastest.
Rescaling the gradient when its overall size is above a limit, so one unusually large step cannot destabilize training. The tiny GPT clips the global norm to 1.0.
Data that is not used for training and is kept aside to measure how well the model works on new text.
Running a trained model to produce outputs, with no weight updates.
A model further tuned on instruction and answer examples so that it follows requests in a chat format.
In attention, the vector that a token offers to be matched against queries.
An operation that rescales each token's vector to zero mean and unit variance across its features, then applies a learned gain and bias.
The size of each optimizer step. A value that is too large makes training unstable, and one that is too small makes it slow.
The raw, unnormalized scores a model outputs for each token in its vocabulary. Softmax turns them into probabilities.
Low-rank adaptation. The frozen weight matrix W is kept, and a trainable low-rank update B times A is added to it.
A number that measures how wrong the model is on a batch of data. Training aims to lower it.
A two-layer feed-forward network applied to each token's vector separately. In the tiny GPT it widens the vector to four times its size and then projects it back.
The negative natural log of the probability the model gave to the correct answer. It is 0 when that probability is 1 and grows as the probability falls.
The situation where training loss keeps falling while validation loss rises, so the model is memorizing the training text rather than learning general patterns.
The exponential of the average negative log-likelihood. A uniform model over 65 characters has a perplexity of 65.
A block layout that applies LayerNorm to the input of each sub-layer and leaves the residual path un-normalized. It makes deep stacks easier to train.
A model whose weights were learned from a large general dataset before you start using or tuning it.
Fine-tuning LoRA adapters on top of a base model stored in 4-bit quantized form, which needs much less memory than full precision.
Storing weights as low-bit integers plus a scale, which reduces memory at the cost of rounding error.
In attention, the vector a token uses to ask which earlier tokens are relevant to it.
Retrieval-augmented generation: find text relevant to a question, paste it into the prompt, and generate an answer from it.
The number of dimensions in a low-rank update. In LoRA, a smaller rank r means fewer trainable parameters.
Adding a layer's input to its output, so information and gradients can pass through the layer unchanged.
Finding the stored texts most relevant to a query, usually by comparing vectors.
Choosing the next token at random according to the model's probabilities, rather than always taking the most likely one.
The float number that converts quantized integers back to real values. In symmetric quantization it is the largest absolute weight divided by the largest integer.
A function that turns a list of numbers into positive values that sum to 1, using exponentials. Larger inputs get larger shares.
A number that divides the logits before softmax. Values below 1 sharpen the distribution and values above 1 flatten it.
A word-weighting scheme that multiplies how often a word appears in a document by how rare the word is across documents. It is a simple stand-in for learned embeddings in retrieval.
A unit that the model reads and predicts, such as a character or a subword piece. Text is turned into a sequence of token ids before the model sees it.
Keeping only the k most likely tokens, renormalizing their probabilities, and sampling from those.
Dividing the data so that most of it is used for training and a held-out part is used to measure progress. The tiny GPT lab uses a 90 to 10 split.
The repeated unit of a GPT, made of an attention sub-layer and an MLP sub-layer, each with a LayerNorm and a residual connection.
In attention, the vector that a token passes on when other tokens attend to it. The output is a weighted sum of values.
The fixed set of tokens a model can read and predict. Its size sets the width of the output layer.
